713209.t: From ὑποκρίνομαι (hupokrínomai, “to play a part on stage”) + -τής (-tḗs).

713287.t: Superlative of the adverb ὕψι (hŭ́psĭ, “on high”).

713288.t: From ὕψι (hŭ́psĭ, “aloft”), probably related to ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”).

713292.t: From a *suh₂-, which, according to the linguist Jay Jasonoff, is a metathesized form from the zero-grade of the root which is to be reconstructed as Proto-Indo-European *sh₂ew- (“to pour, scatter, rain”).

713268.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *sew-? Proto-Indo-European *sewH-? Proto-Indo-European *suH- Proto-Hellenic *hūs Ancient Greek ὗς Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *hūs, from Proto-Indo-European *suH- (“swine”).

713208.t: From ὑποκρίνομαι (hŭpokrī́nomai, “to answer (a fellow actor on stage), play a part, feign, pretend”) + -σις (-sĭs).

713201.t: From ὑποτίθημι (hŭpotĭ́thēmĭ, “to place under, set before, suggest”) + -σις (-sĭs).

713207.t: Mediopassive of ὑποκρίνω (hŭpokrī́nō), from ὑπο- (hŭpo-, “under”) + κρίνω (krī́nō, “to separate, judge, decide”).

713275.t: From Proto-Indo-European *webʰ- (“to weave”), and therefore related distantly to Old English wefan (whence English weave), Sanskrit उ॒भ्नाति॑ (ubhnā́ti, “entwine”), Persian بافتن (bâftan), Tocharian A wäp- (“weave”).

713285.t: From ὕψι (hŭ́psi, “high”), ὕψος (hŭ́psos, “height; summit”) + -λός (-lós). Compare Proto-Celtic *ouxselos, whence Old Irish úasal, Welsh uchel and the first part of Gaulish Uxellodunum.

713274.t: from Proto-Indo-European *údteros (“higher; outer”) from *úd (“upwards; away”); cognate with English outer, utter, Sanskrit उत्त॑र (úttara, “upper; higher”).

713269.t: From some Semitic source. Compare Akkadian 𒍪𒌑𒁍 (/⁠zūpu⁠/), Jewish Palestinian Aramaic אֵיזוֹבָא (ʾēzôḇa), Hebrew אֵזוֹב (ʾēzṓḇ), Classical Syriac ܙܘܦܐ (zōṗā).

713234.t: From the future stem of ὑφοράω (hŭphoráō, “to suspect”) + -εύω (-eúō).

713280.t: From ὑφάζω (hŭphắzō, “to weave”, from ὑφαίνω (hŭphaínō, “to weave”) + -άζω (-ắzō, verbal suffix)) + -μα (-mă, nominal suffix).

713271.t: From ὑστερέω (husteréō, “to come late, to lag behind; to fail to obtain, to lack”) + -μα (-mă, nominal suffix), from ὕστερος (hústeros, “latter, later”) + -έω (-éō, verbal suffix).

713235.t: From ὑπο- (hupo-) + ὀπ- (op-, suppletive root of ὁράω (horáō)) + -τος (-tos).

713256.t: From ὑπο- (hupo-, “hypo-, sub-”) + φέρω (phérō, “to bear, carry”). Exact cognate with Latin sufferō (“to carry under, suffer”).
